subject: Initial DPA scoping, eSign route & data residency questions
messages:
From: Alexandra Rivera <a.rivera@sentinelcloud.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@sentinelcloud.com
Date: Fri, 22 May 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: DPA request & initial scope questions

Hi Vanessa,

Thanks for the quick chat earlier this week. Procurement asked me to start the DPA intake so we can align on subprocessors and the eSign flow before legal gets involved. A few specific asks to kick off: 

- Can you send your standard DPA template (trackable redlineable format preferred)?
- Who are the subprocessors that will process customer data (cloud infra, telemetry, analytics)? We need a shortlist for our reviewer.
- Is DocuSign or Adobe Sign preferred for execution? Our procurement team has an Adobe Sign enterprise account.
- Any restrictions on data residency or EU export controls we should be aware of for US-based production?

If possible, attach a simple dataflow matrix and any SOC2 or audit evidence summaries. Procurement would like to stand up the initial redline review by next Tuesday (May 26).

Appreciate it —
Alexandra
Alexandra Rivera
Head of Procurement
Sentinel Cloud Tech

(Attachment: SCTL_Security_Questionnaire.pdf)

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>
To: Alexandra Rivera <a.rivera@sentinelcloud.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 22 May 2026 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: DPA request & initial scope questions

Hi Alexandra —

Thanks for outlining this. I've attached our current DPA template (Redwood_DPA_Template_v1.2.pdf) and a compact dataflow matrix so your team can map systems quickly. Quick answers inline below and next steps at the end.

- Subprocessors: Primary infra is AWS (us-west-2) via our Dedicated pools; we use VectorMetrics for anonymous telemetry aggregation, and Lookout Analytics (third-party) for cost/usage reports. Full subprocessor list is in section 6 of the attached DPA draft.
- eSign: We support both DocuSign and Adobe Sign. DocuSign is our default for self-serve; for enterprise customers we can accept Adobe Sign. If procurement prefers Adobe Sign, please confirm the signer flow (POC email + CC) so legal can prepare the envelope config.
- Data residency: Production instances for your account can be pinned to us-west; we do not store EU customer production data in the EU by default unless requested. If Sentinel requires EU data residency or EU-to-US transfer controls, we will need to lock in region at onboarding and add the relevant clause to the DPA (standard addendum available).

Proposed next steps:
1) Review attached DPA and mark any high-level redlines; if there are vendor-specific clauses (SCCs/equivalent), flag them.
2) Confirm preferred eSign provider and the email(s) that will sign.
3) If you want a short call with Karthik (privacy counsel) and Soojin (security lead), we can schedule Monday morning.

I'll keep this thread and follow up with a HubSpot link for the intake.

Thanks,
Vanessa Ortiz
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
vanessa@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0192

(Attachments: Redwood_DPA_Template_v1.2.pdf, SCTL_Dataflow_Matrix.xlsx)

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>, Alexandra Rivera <a.rivera@sentinelcloud.com>
Cc: Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 25 May 2026 08:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: DPA request & initial scope questions

Hi Alexandra —

Quick note from legal on things we normally expect to see during initial redlines:
- Data transfer mechanism: we can support EU SCCs or exec-level derogations where appropriate; if Sentinel has a DPA annex template please send it over.
- Subprocessors: please confirm whether you treat telemetry as personal data. If so, we'll review VectorMetrics' controls in more detail.
- Liability and indemnity: if there are procurement caps, flag them early.

Vanessa, happy to join the Monday call if procurement wants to walk through clauses. Alexandra, could you confirm Adobe Sign is acceptable for execution? If yes, procurement can send the envelope and we'll sign; otherwise we can send a DocuSign PowerForm link.

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Compliance
Redwood Inference

(On Fri, 22 May 2026 at 10:03 AM Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com> wrote:)

From: Alexandra Rivera <a.rivera@sentinelcloud.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@sentinelcloud.com
Date: Mon, 25 May 2026 15:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: DPA request & initial scope questions

Hi Vanessa, Karthik —

Thanks, that helps. Procurement confirms Adobe Sign is fine. We'll route the DPA through our Adobe workflow and CC legal@sentinelcloud.com. Two quick clarifications before we send the envelope: 

1) Can you add a brief annex stating that production will be pinned to us-west-2 and that backups are stored in us-east-1 only? Procurement requires explicit note of cross-region storage for DR.
2) We'll treat telemetry as aggregated and non-personal by default, but I'll include a short note for legal to confirm.

We'll aim to send the Adobe Sign envelope by EOD Wednesday (May 27). Can you confirm signers at your side? Who should be the Redwood signer on the envelope? 

Appreciate the quick turnaround.

Best,
Alexandra Rivera
Head of Procurement
Sentinel Cloud Tech

(Attachment: SCTL_Security_Notes.pdf)
